From Weird Ocean

Five creatures from the dark

Entries from the current season. Depths are the ranges where each animal is usually recorded.

  1. NO. 01600–800 M DOWN

    Barreleye Fish

    Macropinna microstoma

    Its head is a clear dome and it looks straight through its own skull. The two green barrels inside are its eyes. They point up to watch for the silhouettes of prey, then rotate forward when it strikes.

    Depth 600 to 800 mZone Twilight zone

  2. NO. 02600–900 M DOWN

    Vampire Squid

    Vampyroteuthis infernalis

    Neither squid nor octopus. It is the only living animal in its own order. When something threatens it, it pulls its webbed cloak over its head and turns itself inside out, showing rows of soft spines.

    Depth 600 to 900 mZone Oxygen minimum zone

  3. NO. 031,000–3,000 M DOWN

    Gulper Eel

    Eurypharynx pelecanoides

    Mostly mouth. The jaws open like a pelican’s pouch and the stomach behind them stretches, so the eel can swallow prey larger than itself on the rare occasion something that size passes by.

    Depth 1,000 to 3,000 mZone Midnight zone

  4. NO. 04SHALLOW REEFS

    Peacock Mantis Shrimp

    Odontodactylus scyllarus

    The punch accelerates faster than a bullet and boils the water at the point of impact. Its eyes, mounted on stalks, register colours and polarised light that human eyes cannot separate at all.

    Depth Shallow reefsZone Sunlight zone

  5. NO. 051,000–4,000 M DOWN

    Anglerfish

    Himantolophus, the footballfish

    She grows her own fishing rod. The bulb at the end of it holds bioluminescent bacteria, and in water this dark a small light is the only thing worth swimming toward. That is the trap.

    Depth 1,000 to 4,000 mZone Midnight zone

The vampire squid’s scientific name, Vampyroteuthis infernalis, translates as “vampire squid from hell”. It eats nothing but debris falling from the water above it.

From Ocean Wonders

The first two compilations

Ocean Wonders opened with these two episodes. Every later compilation follows the same shape: three animals, one theme, thirty seconds.

01EPISODE

3 Deepest Monsters

The first episode goes below the last of the sunlight and stays there. All three animals live where the water is black and the pressure would crush a submarine hull that was not built for it.

In it: Anglerfish, Gulper Eel, Vampire Squid

02EPISODE

3 Fastest Hunters

Three different kinds of speed. A punch, a chase, and a strike that is over before the prey has moved. The episode compares how fast each one actually is, in numbers.

In it: Mantis Shrimp, Sailfish, Mako Shark

Humpback Whale

Megaptera novaeangliae

A 15-metre animal that sings, and whose songs carry across whole ocean basins. Its flippers are the longest limbs of any animal alive, up to a third of its body length, and engineers have copied their bumpy front edge for turbine blades.

Surface to 200 m · Migrates up to 8,000 km

Green Sea Turtle

Chelonia mydas

It crosses thousands of kilometres of open ocean with no landmarks and arrives back at the beach where it hatched. It reads the Earth’s magnetic field the way a compass needle does, only better.

Surface to 150 m · Navigates by magnetism

Jellyfish

Scyphozoa

No brain, no heart, no bones. Jellyfish have still been in the oceans for more than 500 million years, which means the body plan worked long before fish, let alone dinosaurs, existed.

Every ocean zone · Lineage 500M+ years old
